metadata.file_name: 176. Michael & Kyriakides (2023). Mediating effects of motivation and socioeconomic status on reading achievement: a secondary analysis of PISA 2018.pdf
metadata.title: Mediating effects of motivation and socioeconomic status on reading achievement: a secondary analysis of PISA 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 reading literacy scores for 15-year-olds from 38 European countries (n=237,366) and runs uni-level SEM models separately within each country using EQS 6.4. For the reading achievement outcome, the authors report that they considered only the student weights in the analysis to account for different sampling probabilities, while conducting uni-level SEM (students nested within schools acknowledged but not modeled with multilevel SEM). The paper does not report a specific weight variable name (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT), but it explicitly states that student weights were used. No replicate-weight procedure (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is mentioned, and the analysis is not framed as a machine-learning pipeline that would require weight-aware resampling.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The paper describes plausible value handling for PISA reading (ten plausible values, run 10 times, then averaged with attention to measurement error), but it does not report any explicit strategy for missing data (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion or imputation). Because the analysis relies on SEM/CFA with multiple questionnaire indicators and a reading PV outcome, missingness could occur at both the item/scale level and the PV level; the absence of a documented missing-data rule is a reporting gap that limits reproducibility.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample includes 15-year-old students who participated in PISA 2018 reading. The authors restrict the analysis to European countries: from 41 PISA 2018 participating countries, 38 provided sufficient data for the study, yielding 237,366 students. The paper does not specify additional exclusions beyond the requirement of sufficient data for the mediation model; it also acknowledges that CFA/SEM were conducted within each country and that mediators were excluded when they were not statistically significant in the mediation paths.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Within-country SEM mediation results: expected occupational status mediator in all 38 countries; enjoyment of reading mediator in 37/38 countries; mastery-approach orientation mediator in 11/38 countries. Direct SES→reading effect reduced in all models (exact coefficients reported for some countries, e.g., Belarus: .445 initial to .295 final). Model fit assessed with CFI/RMSEA/SRMR (e.g., Table 2 shows CFI mostly ~.963–.990; RMSEA mostly <.08).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading the study leveraged socioeconomic status (ESCS) and three academic motivation elements—expected occupational status, enjoyment of reading, and mastery-approach orientation—to model reading achievement (PVs) via within-country SEM mediation. It found that expected occupational status consistently mediated the SES–reading relationship across all 38 European countries, enjoyment of reading mediated in almost all countries (37/38), and mastery-approach orientation mediated only in 11 countries, with the direct SES effect reduced in every country model. This indicates that equity-oriented reading interventions that raise students’ occupational expectations and intrinsic enjoyment may help narrow SES-related reading gaps, though the cross-sectional design prevents causal claims.

data.outcome_summary: This secondary analysis uses PISA 2018 reading literacy for 15-year-olds from 38 European countries (n=237,366) to test a theory-driven mediation model linking ESCS to reading achievement through three motivation elements. Reading achievement is based on ten PISA plausible values; the authors run the analysis across plausible values and average results while accounting for measurement error, and they use student weights to address sampling probabilities. Within each country, CFA and multigroup CFA are used to validate the measurement structure, but metric invariance is not supported, so mediation is estimated separately by country using uni-level SEM in EQS 6.4. The mediation results show that expected occupational status mediates the SES–reading relationship in all countries, enjoyment of reading in 37/38, and mastery-approach orientation in 11/38, with the direct SES effect reduced in all models. Limitations include cross-sectional data (no causal inference) and a missing-data strategy that is not reported.
